text.p: Mexican conglomerate Grupo Carso S.A. turned in positive third quarter earnings that showed the company is benefitting from its diversification, analysts said.
Carso reported net profits during the first nine months of 2.38 billion pesos versus a profit of 2.81 billion pesos during the same period the year before.

Although net profits fell, analysts said the year ago figures included the company's holdings in Mexican telephone company Telmex, which Carso spun off into a separate company, Carso Global Telecom, earlier this year.
"It was a very good result, above our expectations," said Santiago Pique, an analyst at Bear Stearns in New York.
Carso's earnings per share during the quarter were 0.68 pesos, in-line with a Reuters survey of industry analysts that forecasted 0.71 pesos.

Sales were up 11 percent year on year at a group level and operating income rose 18 percent, although both were flat compared to the second quarter. Adjusting for the stake in Telmex, income rose 5 percent quarter on quarter, according to Kerry McHugh, an analyst at Goldman Sachs.
McHugh said sales were especially good at cable-maker Condumex and mining firm Nacobre -- both of which also increased their operating margins.

The only potential negatives for the company were weak sales at retailer Sanborns, which analysts said reflects weak consumer demand in Mexico, and continued downshifting of brands at cigarette company Cigatam, analysts said.
